_why: Every file here is output captured from the REAL producer the sensor parses,
committed so a test can never assert a format we merely imagined. The rule is
in TESTING.md ('Parsers of external formats'); tools/fixture_lint.py enforces
that each file listed here exists and that each file here is listed.

note: 38 lines, each copied VERBATIM from one of four captures; nothing is
hand-authored. One capture ran the sandbox image under the engine's own
docker flags (--cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE ... --user 1000:1000),
the rest ran on the host to reach shapes the container run did not produce
(unfinished/resumed splits, accept4, rename/link/unlink, AF_NETLINK, and
an unnamed AF_UNIX peer). The last nine lines are one complete unix-socket
trace in which TWO pids each hold an outstanding unfinished syscall at the
same instant — the case a single-slot rejoin would splice wrongly.
Every probe is a benign script (net/dns/fs/child_process); no bench-dd
fixture was executed and no real credential appears.

tshark-node.json.command: tcpdump -i any -U -Z root -w <pcap>; tshark -r <pcap> -T json -Y 'dns.qry.name or http.request or tls.handshake.extensions_server_name' -2
note: The engine's exact stop_pcap command line, unmodified. All 13 packets the
-Y filter admitted are kept, including the six the parser used to drop.
Traffic is benign loopback: two HTTP requests to a local node server, two
DNS lookups, one TLS ClientHello (openssl s_client -servername), plus the
mDNS/LLMNR packets the -i any capture picked up from the host segment.
Re-indented with json.dumps(indent=1); key order and values are unchanged.
shapes: http layer with the request line as a NESTED key holding http.request.method / http.request.uri
dns layer with dns.qry.name nested under Queries.<question>
a DNS response that also carries Queries.<question>.dns.qry.name (so one lookup yields two packets)
tls layer with tls.handshake.extensions_server_name nested under tls.record.tls.handshake
mdns and llmnr layers that carry dns.qry.name under a layer key that is NOT 'dns'
frame.time_relative as a nanosecond-precision string

redactions._reason: the capture host's hostname leaked into the mDNS/LLMNR queries; replaced with a synthetic name of the same shape

tshark-ssdp.json.command: tcpdump -i any -U -Z root -w <pcap>; tshark -r <pcap> -T json -Y 'dns.qry.name or http.request or tls.handshake.extensions_server_name' -2
note: One packet, kept because it is a THIRD instance of the layer-naming trap:
SSDP is HTTP over UDP, so tshark dissects it with the HTTP dissector, it
matches an http.request filter, and it is filed under the layer key `ssdp`.
Its method is `M-SEARCH` and its URI is `*`, which is also why defaulting a
missing method to "GET" and a missing URI to "/" would have misreported a
real request rather than merely blurred it.
shapes: an ssdp layer carrying http.request / http.request.method / http.request.uri
http.host holding an authority WITH a port (239.255.255.250:1900)

tar-missing-dir.bin.command: tar c -C /work node_modules   # with /work an EMPTY tmpfs
note: tar exits 2 ("node_modules: Cannot stat: No such file or directory") and
still writes these 10240 bytes — all NUL, which is a well-formed EMPTY tar
archive that Python's tarfile opens and extracts without complaint. That is
the input which turned an unchecked exit code into
DependencyProvision(installed=True, package_count=0).
shapes: 10240 NUL bytes: a valid tar archive with zero members
